With Austin Reaves (heel) out, Grimes has taken on a much bigger role and has responded with the best stretch of his career.

He also led his squad in rebounding, notched his seventh double-double of the season and finished with a plus-4 differential in the narrow defeat.

His pass in the final seconds was picked off by LaMelo Ball, leading to Minnesota's winning basket. The third-year center remains one of the league's most dependable rebounders.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.

He has recorded at least six assists in two of his last three outings and six times this season. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

He also might come off the bench, but assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks, he should be up to full speed soon.

news.story: Zubac delivered a dependable performance on both ends of the court and notched his second straight double-double, marking the fourth in his last six appearances. His consistent interior role gives him a clear path to production through rebounds and efficient scoring, as he's averaging 12.5 points and 9.5 boards per game while shooting 55.9 percent from the field in that six-game span.

news.headline: Walter finished with 18 points (7-16 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 1-1 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 38 minutes during Wednesday's 103-99 loss to Washington.
news.story: Walter followed Tuesday's 25-point performance against New York with another productive outing, giving him 43 points and 10 made three-pointers across his last two appearances. More encouraging was his versatility Wednesday, as he also recorded seven rebounds, six assists and three steals while playing a substantial role in Toronto's depleted rotation. news.story: Walter erupted with a season high in scoring while setting a new career best with seven three-pointers. The third-year guard rebounded from a tough two-game stretch in which he shot a combined 4-for-16 (25 percent) from the field and 2-for-12 (16.7 percent) from behind the arc. Walter's performance wasn't enough to keep Toronto from losing a fifth straight game, as the Knicks have now beaten the Raptors 15 consecutive times, per Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca. news.story: Walter poured in a team-high 17 points and five three-pointers in Wednesday's loss to Boston, but he wasn't able to carry that sharpshooting into Thursday's defeat. Walter actually led Toronto in plus-minus at plus-10 in 32 minutes, and although that doesn't typically relate to fantasy production, it means he should continue earning minutes at the very least.

news.headline: Irving had 16 points (6-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt), one rebound, eight assists and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 victory over the Jazz.
news.story: Irving scored all 16 of his points in the first half, making his contributions as a facilitator particularly important as Dallas nearly surrendered an 18-point fourth-quarter lead and ended up grinding out a win. His combination of perimeter shooting and playmaking remains valuable, though his scoring output was modest after looking dominant in the first half. Still, Irving has now scored at least 16 points in four straight games and in seven of his nine appearances this month.

news.headline: Irving supplied 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
news.story: After sitting out the second game of a weekend back-to-back set, Irving returned to action and delivered decent numbers. The veteran point guard has scored in double digits in all 12 of his games this season, and he's contributed at least five boards and five assists in three of his seven November contests, averaging 22.9 points, 4.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 threes and 1.4 steals.

news.headline: Irving (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
news.story: Irving didn't play in Sunday's 131-94 loss to Boston, the second game of a back-to-back for the Mavericks. He will return Wednesday for the meeting with Golden State, likely resulting in Naji Marshall heading back to the bench.

news.story: This NBA week opens with 10 games on the docket and one anticipated season debut from an All Star. Brandon Ingram is expected to make his first appearance of the season for the LA Clippers in their road tilt against the Houston Rockets. news.headline: Grimes logged 13 points (2-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 8-9 FT), five rebounds and seven assists in 35 minutes during Friday's 106-104 victory over the Kings.
news.story: Grimes struggled from the field three days after his career-high 47-point outburst, but he delivered when it counted. His step-back three-pointer with 57 seconds left off a pass from Matisse Thybulle put the Lakers ahead for good. He also excelled at the free-throw line. With Austin Reaves (heel) out, Grimes has taken on a much bigger role and has responded with the best stretch of his career.

news.headline: Gobert accumulated seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 victory over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Gobert started to turn things around Saturday, blocking at least three shots for just the second time this season. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

news.headline: Gobert posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

news.headline: Young accumulated 11 points (3-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 win over Orlando.
news.story: Young has shot just 26 percent over his last five games, averaging 31 minutes. However, he's recorded at least eight assists in four of those contests, maintaining fantasy value through playmaking. His shooting struggles remain concerning, but his established offensive role provides upside.

news.headline: Young provided 16 points (4-13 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 4-4 FT), two rebounds, five assists and three steals across 35 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago.
news.story: Young struggled inside the arc but compensated by connecting on four three-pointers and recording three steals, helping Washington secure its second consecutive win. His scoring has been inconsistent recently, as he has failed to reach the 20-point mark in his last four games since recording a season-high 37 points against Detroit on Nov. 12. Young remains a high-usage offensive option, but his fantasy ceiling depends on both his scoring and playmaking. He's averaging 15.6 points, 7.8 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game since the beginning of November.

signals.detail: Lendeborg supplied useful rebounding production from the starting lineup, collecting five offensive boards in a game where second-chance opportunities proved valuable.

news.headline: Lendeborg posted 12 points (5-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds and three assists in 34 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 victory over the Celtics.
news.story: Lendeborg supplied useful rebounding production from the starting lineup, collecting five offensive boards in a game where second-chance opportunities proved valuable. His shooting efficiency was less impressive, though, as he ended with more field-goal attempts (13) than points scored (12). Even with a down game in scoring, Lendeborg's substantial playing time and ability to contribute on the glass offer encouraging signs for his fantasy outlook. His expanded role makes him valuable across all formats and one of the top rookies in this class.

news.story: Lendeborg struggled to find his shooting touch from the field, but that didn't stop him from contributing elsewhere. He showcased his ability to facilitate Thursday, resulting in a new career high in assists, and he accounted for two of Golden State's seven swats on the night. Lendeborg continues to piece together a strong month, averaging 19.6 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.0 blocks through 10 November appearances.

news.story: Fox will miss his second outing of the regular season due to a right shin contusion. Stephon Castle will operate as the primary ballhandler with Dylan Harper (hip) also sidelined, while Jordan McLaughlin should see increased burn off the Spurs' bench.

news.headline: Fox is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings due to a right shin contusion, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Fox could miss Monday's game due to a shin injury he likely picked up during Saturday's game against the Pelicans. With Dylan Harper (hip) out and Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) questionable, the Spurs could be thin at the lead guard position, leaving more ball-handling responsibilities for Stephon Castle.

news.headline: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
news.story: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence, and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

Gobert is 34 years old and has been doing the same thing statistically for more than a decade. He rebounds, blocks shots and converts the field goals he attempts, and few are consistently better at this. You don't draft Gobert for assists or free throw shooting. You know what you're getting. news.headline: Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and is expected to miss four weeks, Portland announced Friday.
news.story: Morant left Thursday's game early with a hamstring injury, which has since been revealed to be a strain that will result in a month-long absence. The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: Sengun produced 28 points (9-16 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 9-13 FT), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one block and one steal over 36 minutes during Friday's 133-124 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: Sengun bounced back from an abbreviated outing in Indiana with a triple-double, tying his season high in assists. The center is averaging 21.6 points, 9.3 rebounds and 7.0 assists through 15 games.

news.headline: Sengun (eye) is available for Friday's game in Denver, Bennett Durando of The Denver Post reports.
news.story: Sengun was forced out of Wednesday's 119-104 win over the Pacers after getting whacked in the face, but he won't miss any additional game action. Sengun is averaging 21.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 1.0 three-pointers, 1.1 steals and 0.9 blocks per game this season.

news.headline: Sengun (eye) is questionable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
news.story: Sengun suffered a blow to the face during Wednesday's game against Indiana, and his availability is now in jeopardy for Friday's tilt. The Rockets should have another update on the big man closer to tipoff.

news.headline: Simons racked up 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one assist in 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 win over the Bucks.
news.story: After starting his first game of the season Wednesday while Tyrese Maxey dealt with a minor foot injury, Simons shifted back to the second unit and delivered at least 12 points for the fifth time in the last six games. The 27-year-old guard appears to be finding a groove with his new team after signing a two-year deal with the Sixers in July, averaging 15.2 points, 2.8 threes, 1.5 boards and 1.2 assists in 24.3 minutes while shooting 44.7 percent (17-for-38) from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Simons is not in the 76ers' starting lineup against the Bucks on Saturday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
news.story: Tyrese Maxey (foot) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence, so Simons -- who made his first start of the season Wednesday against the Magic -- will revert to the bench for Saturday's contest. Simons has averaged 14.6 points per game while connecting on 56.9 percent of his field-goal attempts over his last five outings, and although he's back to a reserve role, he should still see plenty of opportunities on offense in the continued absence of Jaylen Brown (hamstring).

news.headline: Simons notched 18 points (7-12 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds and two assists across 38 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic.
news.story: Simons has scored in double figures in five of his last six appearances, averaging 14.2 points and 2.3 three-pointers during that stretch. With both Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown sidelined, Simons moved into the starting lineup for the first time this season and benefited from increased playing time and offensive opportunities. Brown's hamstring injury could keep him out for multiple games, giving Simons a chance to maintain an expanded role and offer additional fantasy value in points and three-pointers.

signals.detail: Ingram will start Monday's game against Houston.

news.headline: Ingram will start Monday's game against Houston.
news.story: Ingram has been cleared to make his 2026-27 season debut after recovering from a partially torn Achilles, and he'll do so as a member of the first unit. He'll presumably have his minutes monitored closely Monday, though the team hasn't shared how large of a workload he'll take on in his LA debut.

news.headline: Ingram (Achilles) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Monday's game against the Rockets.
news.story: Shams Charania of ESPN reported that Ingram was expected to make his 2026-27 debut Monday versus Houston, and now his omission from the injury report confirms he will suit up. The 29-year-old, who was traded by the Raptors during the offseason, averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists over 33.8 minutes per tilt in 77 regular-season games for Toronto in 2025-26. Ingram will likely see limited action in his first game back from surgery to repair a partially torn Achilles. He also might come off the bench, but assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks, he should be up to full speed soon.

news.headline: Ingram (Achilles) is expected to make his season and team debut Monday against the Rockets, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
news.story: The star forward is set to make his long-awaited return after undergoing surgery for a partially torn Achilles tendon in May. Ingram, who'll miss Saturday's game in Dallas, is likely to carry a minutes restriction following a lengthy layoff, though his presence is certain to cut into the playing time of the likes of Kris Dunn, Max Strus and Gradey Dick on the wing for the Clippers.

signals.detail: Burries is not in the Bucks' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday.

news.headline: Burries ended with 26 points (12-20 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 0-1 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one block over 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: The 26 points were a career high for the rookie guard, but Burries' big afternoon got overshadowed by Tyler Herro's career-high 50. This was Burries' first game with the second unit since Oct. 31, as Ryan Rollins moved back into the starting five, but the duo saw nearly equal workloads. Coach Taylor Jenkins might continue to mix and match next to Herro in his backcourt as he searches for a lineup that clicks.

news.headline: Burries is not in the Bucks' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday.
news.story: The 2026 10th-overall pick has started in each of the Bucks' last 10 games and has averaged 11.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.3 threes and 0.9 steals over 26.5 minutes in that span. However, Burries will revert to a bench role Saturday while Ryan Rollins enters the Bucks' starting five.

news.headline: Burries accumulated 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Burries has recorded multiple steals in four of his last five appearances, adding defensive value to his growing offensive role. He's attempted at least nine shots in three straight games, suggesting increased confidence and opportunity. However, inconsistent efficiency and Milwaukee's crowded backcourt could limit his fantasy ceiling.

news.headline: Bassey recorded 13 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals across 26 minutes during Sunday's 88-87 victory over the Celtics.
news.story: Bassey finished one rebound shy of a double-double and missed just one of his seven field-goal attempts, but his contributions didn't end there. He also set season highs in assists and steals, making him one of Golden State's best players in this tight win. His long-term consistency will depend on maintaining a meaningful role in the Warriors' frontcourt rotation, though.

news.headline: Bassey ended with 16 points (6-7 FG, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal across 25 minutes during Thursday's 126-98 loss to the Grizzlies.
news.story: Bassey delivered his strongest performance of the season, capitalizing on increased minutes with his first double-double. He's started to establish a larger frontcourt role, combining efficient interior finishing with rebounding and rim protection. His limited offensive involvement caps his ceiling, but consistent minutes could make him a useful category-league streamer.

news.headline: Bassey recorded 10 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 FT), eight rebounds, one block and one steal over 22 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.
news.story: Getting his second start of the season, Bassey fell a couple of boards shy of his second double-double of 2026-27. The 26-year-old center has been taking on a bigger role than expected of late, seeing double-digit minutes in nine straight games (two starts) and averaging 17.4 minutes, 9.4 points, 6.4 boards and 1.0 blocks during that span while shooting 66.0 percent from the floor. news.headline: Brunson contributed 22 points (8-18 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, seven assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 win over the Pacers.
news.story: Brunson didn't need an explosive scoring performance, as Karl-Anthony Towns contributed 30 points and Josh Hart recorded a triple-double. Still, Brunson delivered seven assists and played a big role as the Knicks earned a fifth straight win. His established offensive responsibilities remain intact, although the relatively inefficient perimeter shooting and four turnovers reduced the fantasy value of Sunday's performance. One subpar game -- if it can be called that -- won't reduce his elite fantasy appeal as one of the most productive guards in the league.

news.headline: Brunson supplied 30 points (11-23 FG, 6-10 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds and five assists over 36 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 victory over Portland.
news.story: Brunson got off to a scorching hot start, drilling his first five three-point attempts while racking up 21 points on 10 shots in his first 14 minutes of play. However, his hot shooting didn't carry over after halftime, and he went scoreless in the fourth quarter. Still, his 30 points were a game high, and he helped the Knicks notch their fourth straight win.

news.headline: Brunson amassed 21 points (8-20 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, seven assists and two steals in 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 win over the Timberwolves.
news.story: Brunson wasn't particularly efficient inside the arc, but his four three-pointers helped compensate for an 8-for-20 shooting performance. He's now scored at least 20 points in eight straight games, surpassing the 30-point mark four times over that stretch. Brunson should continue to be the alpha on the Knicks' offensive scheme, though at times he'll operate as the No. 2 option when Karl-Anthony Towns takes over, as he did Thursday.

news.headline: James finished with 23 points (8-13 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), six rebounds and three assists in 30 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
news.story: James pieced together an efficient scoring line and led the Sixers with 23 points, though it wasn't enough to help Philly secure a sixth consecutive victory. He was particularly sharp from beyond the arc, which is a welcome sight considering he was hitting at a clip of 21.7 percent from deep in his first 13 games of the 2026-27 campaign entering Monday. James has put up 20-plus points in three straight appearances and continues to produce across the board, averaging 5.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.0 steals over this brief stretch.

news.headline: James contributed 21 points (9-14 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, six assists, one block and three steals over 35 minutes during Saturday's 132-129 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: The Sixers fielded a very balanced offense on the afternoon, with all five starters plus two bench players scoring at least 12 points, and James' 21 was second only to Joel Embiid's 26. James has topped 20 points in back-to-back games and three times in his last five appearances, a stretch in which the 41-year-old slam-dunk Hall of Famer is averaging 18.2 points, 6.6 assists, 5.8 boards, 0.8 steals and 0.8 threes in 32.2 minutes.

news.headline: George (rest) isn't listed on the injury report for Tuesday's game against the Wizards, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
news.story: George didn't suit up for Sunday's loss to the Warriors in the second leg of a back-to-back set, though he'll return to action Tuesday. The veteran forward has averaged 18.8 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.0 steals in 30.2 minutes per showing over his last five outings, and his return will leave fewer minutes available for guys like Jordan Walsh, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser.

news.headline: George (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
news.story: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser could all see increased burn. George will likely return for Tuesday's game at Washington.

news.headline: George finished Saturday's 97-96 loss to Sacramento with 19 points (6-21 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 5-6 FT), eight rebounds, five assists, one block and four steals over 37 minutes.
news.story: George struggled with his shot but made up for it with an excellent all-around statistical contribution, especially on defense. With Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) out, George embraced a bigger offensive role and attempted a team-high 21 shots. His five combined steals and blocks were especially valuable in category formats, showing he can stay productive even when his shooting efficiency suffers.

news.headline: Reed finished Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Hawks with 16 points (6-11 FG, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes.
news.story: Reed has averaged 12.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.6 steals, 1.0 blocks and 24.3 minutes over his last five games. His efficient interior scoring and defensive versatility provide dependable fantasy value despite fluctuating playing time.

news.headline: Reed produced 17 points (7-9 FG, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 win over New Orleans.
news.story: Reed recorded his third-best scoring output of the season and finished just three boards shy of his third double-double. Reed continues to perform at a high level despite being entrenched in a bench role, as John Collins has been starting at center with Jalen Duren (hamstring) sidelined. Reed is averaging 11.1 points, 8.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists and a combined 1.8 steals-plus-blocks per game off the bench this season.

signals.detail: Hauser will start in Saturday's game against Sacramento.

news.headline: Hauser will start in Saturday's game against Sacramento.
news.story: Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (shoulder) won't play, so Hauser will get the start Saturday night. In Hauser's only start of the 2026-27 campaign, which was in the 109-102 win over Milwaukee on Nov. 4, he finished with 11 points and two rebounds across 30 minutes.

news.headline: Hauser contributed 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), one rebound and two assists in 25 minutes during Monday's 115-105 loss to the Magic.
news.story: Hauser connected on four three-pointers, matching his season-high with 12 points. It's been a relatively underwhelming season thus far for Hauser, serving as nothing more than a potential streaming option for anyone needing a boost in perimeter scoring. He has played more than 25 minutes only once in 14 games, an indication that nothing is likely to change, barring injuries to other players.

news.headline: Hauser ended Tuesday's 123-101 victory over Philadelphia with 12 points (4-6 FG, 4-6 3Pt), five rebounds and two assists across 18 minutes.
news.story: The 12 points were a season-high output for Hauser, and this was the fifth time this season he's notched double-digit points. The 18-minute workload restricted his overall fantasy ceiling, but Hauser remains a specialist in three-point shooting, so he's better suited to be a waiver-wire pickup in category-based leagues rather than in standard formats.

news.headline: Da Silva racked up 12 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt) and two rebounds in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: Da Silva has attempted just 13 shots over his last two games after averaging 15.7 across his previous three appearances. His improved efficiency hasn't offset the reduced offensive involvement, while limited defensive production further restricts his fantasy ceiling. Paolo Banchero's (ankle) eventual return could squeeze his opportunities further.

news.headline: Da Silva isn't starting Monday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Da Silva started Friday's game against Milwaukee due to Jalen Suggs coming off the bench in his return from a knee injury, but Suggs will return to the first unit for Monday's clash. Da Silva is averaging 15.8 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in his last five appearances as a reserve.

news.headline: Da Silva will start Friday's game against the Bucks.
news.story: Jalen Suggs (knee) will come off the bench in his return to action, opening the door for da Silva to join the first unit in his return from a two-game absence due to a calf strain. Over his last five appearances (one start), the 25-year-old forward has averaged 15.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 31.8 minutes per showing.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Carter has scored in double figures in three consecutive games, averaging 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds during that stretch. The veteran center has also connected on multiple three-pointers for the first time in November, providing an additional dimension to his offensive production. news.story: George came crashing back to earth after back-to-back 30-point games against the two Los Angeles teams. He went cold from deep, and his late turnover ended any hope of a comeback. news.headline: Edgecombe totaled 24 points (8-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds, six assists and two steals in 43 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 victory over the Magic.
news.story: Edgecombe stepped up with Tyrese Maxey (foot), Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Dean Wade (hamstring) sidelined, scoring 13 points in the fourth quarter to help Philadelphia erase a 17-point deficit. The second-year guard has scored in double figures in four straight games, averaging 16.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 6.0 assists during that stretch. His ability to contribute across multiple categories gives him strong fantasy appeal, particularly if Philadelphia continues to operate with a depleted starting lineup.

news.headline: Edgecombe registered 24 points (8-15 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds, six assists, two steals and four turnovers across 43 minutes in Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic.
news.story: Edgecombe delivered 13 of his 24 points during the final frame, and he came through with some clutch buckets down the stretch to help the 76ers erase a 17-point deficit. The second-year shooting guard is averaging 13.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 1.7 triples and 1.7 steals per game this season, which has been good enough for top-40 value in fantasy leagues.

news.headline: McDaniels notched 34 points (12-16 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, six assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Monday's 142-116 win over Brooklyn.
news.story: McDaniels followed up his season-high 25-point outing Saturday by setting a new career high in scoring two days later. He was uber-efficient from everywhere, missing just four shots while tallying a season-high 10 boards. McDaniels recorded his first double-double of the 2026-27 campaign and should continue delivering stellar fantasy production across the board.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 25 points (11-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal across 36 minutes in Saturday's 104-95 win over Memphis.
news.story: McDaniels ended the night by recording a season high in scoring. The 27-year-old has had a quality 2026-27 campaign, averaging 17.5 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists, all career bests, along with 1.2 steals over 33.9 minutes per contest in 17 regular-season games. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined indefinitely, McDaniels is in an excellent position to remain more productive than in previous seasons.

news.headline: Hunter posted 30 points (12-16 FG, 5-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), six rebounds, two assists and one block across 37 minutes during Friday's 106-104 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: Hunter erupted for a season high, easily topping his previous best and knocking down nearly everything he threw up. His layup with under two minutes left tied the game, though the Kings couldn't hold on. It was a big bounce-back after a rough shooting night against Phoenix on Wednesday.

news.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as available for Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Hunter was listed as questionable ahead of this contest, but he will avoid his third absence of the 2026-27 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in 12 regular-season games, averaging 13.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists over 32.8 minutes per outing.

news.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Hunter has been bothered by left hip soreness. While it kept him off the floor for Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, he returned for Wednesday's meeting with the Suns. If Hunter can't suit up Friday, it could mean more minutes for Leaky Black and Alex Karaban.

news.story: Castle finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama, who led the way with 50 points, and Castle was particularly deadly from beyond the arc. Four of his five three-pointers came during a third-quarter stretch that helped San Antonio pull away for good. Castle's ability to contribute as both a scorer and facilitator gives him multiple paths to fantasy value, while efficient perimeter shooting adds another dimension to his offensive profile.

news.story: Castle's 12 assists were particularly impressive considering he shared the backcourt with De'Aaron Fox, who was limited to 10 points and five dimes in 32 minutes. With Dylan Harper (undisclosed) listed as day-to-day, Castle could see even more ball-handling duties in the coming games.

news.story: Risacher was productive inside the arc and on the glass despite missing all five of his three-point attempts. His eight rebounds were particularly useful, giving him a respectable fantasy line. The third-year forward continues to offer complementary production in Dallas' rotation, but his limited playmaking and inconsistent outside shooting can restrict his value. He seems to be trending in the right direction, scoring double-digit points in four of his last six appearances while averaging 12.3 points and 5.2 boards per game in that span.

Still, Risacher has posted his two highest-scoring totals of the season over the last three games, suggesting he is finding his footing.

news.story: Quickley's seven assists led Toronto, but his scoring has been relatively modest in the two consecutive meetings with New York, with him totaling 31 points on 13-for-29 shooting combined. With Scottie Barnes back in the lineup, Quickley has another established ball handler alongside him, but his ability to contribute as both a scorer and facilitator should help maintain his offensive role.

news.headline: Wilson is undergoing surgery for a fractured right hand and will miss at least four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis offensively going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value for the next month or so.

news.headline: Wilson won't return to Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a right hand injury. He'll finish with 15 points (5-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes.
news.story: Wilson turned in an efficient performance en route to 15 points before exiting Wednesday's contest early in the third quarter. The rookie forward's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game against Atlanta. If he's forced to miss time, Leonard Miller, Patrick Williams and Noa Essengue would be candidates for increased minutes.

news.headline: Wilson exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Wednesday's game against San Antonio due to an apparent hand injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
news.story: Wilson was spotted holding his hand while heading back to the locker room. The rookie forward can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

news.story: We're roughly a month into the NBA season, and some fantasy managers are already regretting decisions they made on draft day. Now is a good time to see if those managers are willing to make a deal. When evaluating potential trade targets, I pay close attention to minutes, shot attempts and shooting percentages. I'm much more inclined to trade for a player who's struggling to make shots than one who's getting fewer of them. news.headline: White finished Friday's 111-97 loss to Atlanta with 11 points (5-17 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 1-1 FT), nine assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block over 26 minutes.
news.story: It was a tough shooting night for White, who failed to connect on any of his five attempts from beyond the arc. His volume from the field was enough for him to extend his double-digit points streak to five games, and his nine dimes tied a season high that he set against the Cavaliers in Nov. 9. Over his last five outings, White has averaged 16.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.2 threes and 0.8 steals over 22.3 minutes per game.

news.headline: White closed with 19 points (6-12 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-7 FT), three rebounds, four assists and three steals in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
news.story: White has found his groove since returning from a calf injury that cost him the start of the season, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games. His fadeaway jumper in the final minute of regulation put Charlotte in front, but a missed free throw shortly after left the door open. His minutes are still being managed, but the guard who signed a three-year, $74 million deal this summer is clearly rounding into form.

news.headline: Williams will start Sunday's game against the Heat, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
news.story: The Thunder have a lengthy injury report for Sunday's meeting with Miami, so Williams will enter the starting lineup. However, with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck) sidelined, there is room for Williams to be more involved offensively.

news.headline: Jaquez is in the Bucks' starting lineup against the 76ers on Saturday.
news.story: Jaquez has come off the bench for each of the Bucks' last five games, but he'll rejoin the starting five along with Ryan Rollins while Brayden Burries and Nate Ament move to bench roles. Jaquez started in each of Milwaukee's first 11 games of the regular season and averaged 15.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 threes and 0.5 steals over 27.5 minutes per contest in that span.

news.headline: Jaquez finished Thursday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers with nine points (3-11 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two assists, one rebound and one steal across 22 minutes.
news.story: Jaquez struggled with efficiency off the bench once again, and he's shot just 32.0 percent from the field over the last three games. The fourth-year swingman has scored single-digit points in two of those three outings, during which he's averaged 8.3 points, 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals across 25.0 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Jaquez supplied 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds and five assists over 23 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 loss to the Heat.
news.story: Jaquez has scored just 16 points over his last two games after consecutive 20-point performances. His five assists Wednesday provided some value, but moving to the bench has reduced his offensive opportunities. He's maintained a rotation role, though inconsistent shot volume makes him a volatile fantasy option.

news.headline: Reed finished Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Hawks with 16 points (6-11 FG, 4-4 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes.
news.story: Reed has averaged 12.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 1.6 steals, 1.0 blocks and 24.3 minutes over his last five games. His efficient interior scoring and defensive versatility provide dependable fantasy value despite fluctuating playing time.

news.headline: Reed produced 17 points (7-9 FG, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 20 minutes during Wednesday's 122-109 win over New Orleans.
news.story: Reed recorded his third-best scoring output of the season and finished just three boards shy of his third double-double. Reed continues to perform at a high level despite being entrenched in a bench role, as John Collins has been starting at center with Jalen Duren (hamstring) sidelined. Reed is averaging 11.1 points, 8.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists and a combined 1.8 steals-plus-blocks per game off the bench this season.

news.headline: Larsson finished Sunday's 123-113 win over Oklahoma City with 21 points (9-14 FG, 3-7 3Pt), three rebounds, five assists and three steals across 30 minutes.
news.story: Larsson bounced back from a four-point outing in his return from illness, matching his season high in scoring. He's averaged 25.4 minutes per contest over his last five appearances (four starts), but Sunday's expanded workload and defensive contributions strengthen his fantasy appeal if his minutes stabilize.

news.headline: Larsson ended with four points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 15 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: Larsson returned to the starting lineup after missing three consecutive games due to an illness, but his playing time was significantly reduced. The third-year forward averaged 12.0 points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists across his previous three appearances before the absence. His minutes will be worth monitoring as he works his way back into Miami's rotation, though his limited offensive involvement makes him a risky fantasy option in standard leagues.

news.headline: Larsson (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Larsson is set to return from a three-game absence due to an illness. With the 25-year-old wing back in the lineup, there will be fewer minutes available for the likes of Tim Hardaway and Myron Gardner (hamstring). Larsson has averaged 10.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 steals across 29.4 minutes per game in his last five outings (two starts).

news.headline: Bridges contributed 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 victory over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: While Bridges' numbers from Saturday's game don't jump off the page, he came through when it mattered most for New York, drilling a buzzer-beating triple to save the day for the Knicks after they blew a 26-point lead. The 30-year-old veteran is averaging 7.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.1 triples and 1.1 steals per game this season.

news.headline: Bridges totaled eight points (3-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, one block and two steals across 31 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 victory over the Timberwolves.
news.story: Bridges contributed three defensive stats despite limited offensive involvement. His scoring has dipped below double figures in three of the past five games, making steals and perimeter shooting increasingly important to his fantasy value. His secure minutes provide some stability.

news.headline: Bridges totaled 17 points (7-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 30 minutes during Tuesday's 111-102 win over the Raptors.
news.story: After scoring just five points on 2-for-5 shooting in Sunday's win over Toronto, Bridges was more aggressive in hunting his shot and turned in an efficient outing. The veteran swingman finished as the Knicks' second-leading scorer and has now dropped 17-plus points in two of his last three games, averaging 13.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 30.3 minutes per showing during that span.

news.headline: Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Duren hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right hamstring strain, though he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. news.headline: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

news.headline: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.

Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

news.story: Sengun bounced back from an abbreviated outing in Indiana with a triple-double, tying his season high in assists. The center is averaging 21.6 points, 9.3 rebounds and 7.0 assists through 15 games.

news.headline: Sengun (eye) is available for Friday's game in Denver, Bennett Durando of The Denver Post reports.
news.story: Sengun was forced out of Wednesday's 119-104 win over the Pacers after getting whacked in the face, but he won't miss any additional game action. Sengun is averaging 21.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 1.0 three-pointers, 1.1 steals and 0.9 blocks per game this season.

news.headline: Sengun (eye) is questionable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
news.story: Sengun suffered a blow to the face during Wednesday's game against Indiana, and his availability is now in jeopardy for Friday's tilt. The Rockets should have another update on the big man closer to tipoff.

news.story: Flagg delivered the decisive moment for the Mavericks, converting two free throws with 3.7 seconds remaining after Utah erased a substantial fourth-quarter deficit. The second-year forward led the Mavericks in scoring and took an aggressive approach, drawing 10 free-throw attempts and making nine. His expanding offensive responsibilities continue to support his fantasy appeal, and while the five turnovers weren't ideal, fantasy managers can live with them given everything else he brings to the table. news.story: Hunter erupted for a season high, easily topping his previous best and knocking down nearly everything he threw up. His layup with under two minutes left tied the game, though the Kings couldn't hold on. It was a big bounce-back after a rough shooting night against Phoenix on Wednesday.

news.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as available for Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Hunter was listed as questionable ahead of this contest, but he will avoid his third absence of the 2026-27 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in 12 regular-season games, averaging 13.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists over 32.8 minutes per outing.

news.headline: Hunter (hip) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Hunter has been bothered by left hip soreness. While it kept him off the floor for Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, he returned for Wednesday's meeting with the Suns. If Hunter can't suit up Friday, it could mean more minutes for Leaky Black and Alex Karaban.

news.story: Walter followed Tuesday's 25-point performance against New York with another productive outing, giving him 43 points and 10 made three-pointers across his last two appearances. More encouraging was his versatility Wednesday, as he also recorded seven rebounds, six assists and three steals while playing a substantial role in Toronto's depleted rotation. news.story: Walter poured in a team-high 17 points and five three-pointers in Wednesday's loss to Boston, but he wasn't able to carry that sharpshooting into Thursday's defeat. Walter actually led Toronto in plus-minus at plus-10 in 32 minutes, and although that doesn't typically relate to fantasy production, it means he should continue earning minutes at the very least.

news.headline: McDaniels notched 34 points (12-16 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 10 rebounds, six assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Monday's 142-116 win over Brooklyn.
news.story: McDaniels followed up his season-high 25-point outing Saturday by setting a new career high in scoring two days later. He was uber-efficient from everywhere, missing just four shots while tallying a season-high 10 boards. McDaniels recorded his first double-double of the 2026-27 campaign and should continue delivering stellar fantasy production across the board.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 25 points (11-17 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists and one steal across 36 minutes in Saturday's 104-95 win over Memphis.
news.story: McDaniels ended the night by recording a season high in scoring. The 27-year-old has had a quality 2026-27 campaign, averaging 17.5 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists, all career bests, along with 1.2 steals over 33.9 minutes per contest in 17 regular-season games. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined indefinitely, McDaniels is in an excellent position to remain more productive than in previous seasons.

news.story: Brown is set to return from a two-game absence, which should result in Kentavious Caldwell-Pope heading back to the second unit. Brown is averaging 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.9 triples and 1.3 steals per game this season.

news.headline: Brown (hamstring) is listed as probable for Monday's game versus Portland.
news.story: Brown has a left hamstring strain, though it appears he will suit up after missing only two games. It's unclear if he will see limited action in his first game back from the brief layoff. However, Brown's return would leave fewer minutes available for Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker.

news.headline: George supplied 15 points (4-9 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), five rebounds and seven assists over 26 minutes during Sunday's 116-114 loss to Dallas.
news.story: George provided balanced production despite playing fewer than 27 minutes, and while Utah's remarkable comeback was driven primarily by Svi Mykhailiuk's perimeter shooting, George still made his presence felt -- he was Utah's third-leading scorer and paced the team in assists. His role as a playmaker and scorer gives him a solid fantasy floor even in games in which his shooting volume isn't very high. His nine field-goal attempts Sunday were a season-low mark.

news.headline: George finished Friday's 111-101 loss to the Suns with 14 points (4-17 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), three rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes.
news.story: George came crashing back to earth after back-to-back 30-point games against the two Los Angeles teams. He went cold from deep, and his late turnover ended any hope of a comeback. Off nights like this will happen with Lauri Markkanen (hand) out and defenses keying in on George. He is still averaging 21.6 points and 7.1 assists as Utah's go-to floor general.

news.headline: George supplied 30 points (9-17 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 7-9 FT), one rebound, 10 assists and one steal in 39 minutes during Wednesday's 109-97 victory over the Lakers.
news.story: George was instrumental in Utah's second consecutive upset, scoring nine points in the fourth quarter to help end Los Angeles' nine-game winning streak.
